links.reason: Verse 35 states the doctrine in general (கறங்கென வினையினோடிக் ... பிறவிகள் பேச லாகா) and 199 has the reborn kid say யான் விளைத்த வினைப்பயன் இன்னதே; the second is one instance of the first. The pairing is illustration of a doctrine by its own story, and teaches only restates that the doctrine is 'lived', naming no test, limit or cost.
links.text_issue: 199 line 4 is ambiguous between the wealth and the fallen state as the fruit.

links.reason: The verbal answer is real: 306's ஒண் பொன் குன்றம் தலை திறந்திட்டு ... ஏற்பார்க்கு ... ஈமின் is fulfilled in 331's செம் பொன் குன்று எனப் பெரு நல நிதி தலை திறந்து ... இரவலர்க்கு ஆர்த்தி. But teaches says the giver 'believes the child his own', while திருமகன் பெற்று என says he acts as though he had begotten a son, so he knows he did not.
links.text_issue: 331 line 4 (செருநிலம் பயப்பு உற) is unclear as printed.

links.reason: Both verses use fire, but 110 has Yugi set the town alight (யூகி ... ஊரிற்றீ யிடுவித்தான்) while 141 names no one and shows only burnt ornaments and a grieving king. That 141's fire is Yugi's device comes from the plot, not the verse, so 'his habit' is not shown by the pair; a recurring plot device is not a meaningful shared image.

The link rests on the stock epithet of a sea-like army: 554 வேற்கடற் றானை வேந்தர் and 813 மன்னர் தங்கள் கடற்படை. 554 is the king's hyperbolic refusal of suitors even if they begged, and 813 is a rout in battle; nothing in 813 turns the refusal into fact or answers it.

Both prefaces plead that meaning outweighs a flawed vehicle: UKK 3 the cloth bundle kept with the gem (மணிபொதி கிழி ... மணியுடன் நன்கு வைப்பார்), NKK 3 the lamp not thrown out for its smoke (புகைக்கொடி ... விளக்கை இகழ்ச்சியின் நீப்பாரில்லை). The agreement is a known apology convention, and teaches only names the convention plus a change of object. UKK 3 line 4 (இரங்கல் செல்லாம்) says the poet need not grieve, not that he asks for pity.

695 is the minister's plan (மாயங் காட்டி ... சீயந் தன்மேற் கொளப்புணர்த் திடுவன்) and 696 the next step of the same plan, commissioning Arikethu (மாயச் சீயமாகென வகுத்து விட்டான்). This is plot sequence in adjacent verses, which the graph already records; nothing is answered or reversed.

Both make the ruler a driver whose skill decides whether the vehicle survives, and they share the verb of knowing how: 2909 ஊர்நிலம் அறிதல் தேற்றாது ஊருமேல் முறிந்து வீழும் against Puram 185 உய்த்தல் தேற்றான் ஆயின் ... அள்ளற் பட்டு. 2909 adds the ground itself (நேர்நிலத்து, ஊர்நிலம்) as what must be known, which the Sangam cart lacks, so both gains clauses hold.
links.text_issue: The marked reading's 'ploughed field' for நேர்நிலத்து should be 'level ground'; this does not touch the link.

links.reason: Both use the same picture of one richly fed who now begs (Nal. 1 அறுசுவை உண்டி ... சென்றிரப்பர் ஓரிடத்துக் கூழ்; 2624 அம்பொற் கலத்துள் அடுபால் ... பிச்சை யெனக்கூறி) and draw the same moral (செல்வம் ஒன்று உண்டாக வைக்கற்பாற் றன்று; நம்பன்மின் செல்வ). The epic does not limit the quatrain; it adds a cause (வெவ்வினை) and a turn to dharma (நல்லறமே நினைமின்), which is development, so qualifies is the wrong type.

The tension is one of words only: Soolamani 560's கேவலப் பெண் is the Jain kevala knowledge, while Tirumanthiram 494's கேவலத்து ஆரது விட்டவர் uses the Siddhanta term for the soul's state under anava alone. The two texts make no claims about the same thing, so this is a homonym across schools, not an incompatible claim. The Tirumanthiram gains nothing about its own doctrine.

The epic does not limit Kural 259 (அவிசொரிந் தாயிரம் வேட்டலின் ... உயிர்செகுத் துண்ணாமை நன்று); it condemns the flesh rite as the couplet does, so the link is agreement or development. Teaches says 'the dead eat the dead', but in 196 the brahmins (நான்மறை யாளரே) eat and bless the dead king. That the meat is the reborn king himself comes from the next verse, not from 196.

The elephant image is close: 1831 பாகரும் வெருவரக் கொன்றிட ... கந்து அணைவு இன்றி against Maduraikanchi 381-383 கோலோர்க் கொன்று ... காழ்சாய்த்துக் கந்துநீத் துழிதரும் கடாஅ யானை. But the circling drill and the 'two stages of one hero's mastery' rest on verse 1839, which is not in the packet, and a musth elephant killing its handlers is a stock image. The epic-side gain, that it 'draws on' the Sangam catalogue, is an influence claim the words do not establish.

The echo is real: 2290 வெள்வேல் ஒய்யெனப் பறித்து நக்கான் shares the act and its words (வேல், பறி, நகு) with Kural 774 மெய்வேல் பறியா நகும். But teaches rests the laugh's cause on the foe's choice of target in 2289, which the packet does not print. 2290 itself gives no cause, so the claimed addition to the couplet cannot be checked here.

Both poems use Balarama's whiteness: Kar Narpathu 19 நாஞ்சில் வலவன் நிறம்போல for the maraa blossom that sends the man's heart ahead (நெடுவிடைச் சென்றதென் னெஞ்சு), and Thinaimalai 96 ஆழியான் ... தம்முன் ... ஆய்நிறம் for moonlight that is வேல்போலும் to the partnerless. The same divine colour marks longing fulfilled in one and pain in the other, which neither poem shows alone.

Kural 685 asks the envoy to remove what offends (தூவாத நீக்கி), and Soolamani 1210 has envoys who brought தீதுரை that burned the ears (செவிகள் சுட்ட) yet are let go by ancient custom (தூதுவர் முறைப்படுந் தொன்மையால் ... பொறுக்கல் வேண்டும்). The epic adds a case the couplet does not foresee: the immunity holds even when the office is failed. Both gains are specific.

The contrast is partly real: Kural 1263 sets his resolve as his companion (உள்ளம் துணையாக) apart from her, and Kar Narpathu 7 names his aims of giving and punishing (நச்சியார்க் கீதலு நண்ணார்த் தெறுதலும்). But in the venba the guarantee of return is the rain (தரூஉம் ... மழை), not the motive, so teaches overstates when it makes the motive itself 'a guarantee'.

Both refuse the straying man's chest with the same words: 2722 பரத்தையர்த் தோய்ந்த மார்பம் பத்தினி மகளிர் தீண்டார, Kural 1311 நண்ணேன் பரத்த நின் மார்பு. The couplet's grounds are only being looked at (கண்ணின் பொதுஉண்பர), while the monkey's are an actual lying-with (தோய்ந்த). The pair shows the sulk against a real cause, and both gains hold.
links.text_issue: 2722 line 2 (the bath of clear water) is not clear as printed.

links.reason: 1259 has the camp pitched on Arungalam hill (அருங்கலப் பெயர்கொள் குன்றின்மேல் பாடி விட்டனன்), and 1266 has the armies meet (எதிர் ஊன்றி ஏற்றதே). This is battle-narrative sequence; the choice of ground plays no part in 1266, so nothing is fulfilled.

Calling these a tension stretches them. 3033's bees lament that the hair and garland they lived by are gone (நுங்கடை நோக்கிநாம் வாழும் வாக்கையம்), a poet's conceit that argues nothing against renunciation, and Siddhar 329 lists what suffices to the renouncer. There is no incompatible claim, only a difference of tone, and the bees' loss is not a 'cost' that tests the Siddhar.

Soolamani 254 is a king thanking ministers for their service (என்னைநீர் இறைவனாக்கி), and CC 206 is a counsellor pressing an absorbed king (காவல குறிப்பு அன்றேனும் ... கேண்மோ). These are different situations sharing only the theme of king and counsel. Neither limits the other, and the 'willing king' moral is read into the pair.

The vow and its keeping are real: 714 நின்னையும் மாலையாலே ... யாப்பன் is fulfilled in 738 செம்பொன் மாலை ... ஆகத்துப் பூட்டி. But teaches adds that the result was settled 'before a string was touched'. In 714 she is already moved by him (என் உள்ளம் யாத்தாய்) and asks for a short wait (சிறிது இடைப் படுக), so the verse does not place her vow before the playing.

210's வன்பொறி யானை விட்டேன் owns a contrived elephant, and 39 describes one made of lac, wax thread, wood, hair and hide. That 39's makers are Pradyotan's side is not stated in 39 (தாமியற்றினார் has no named subject), and the marker's own nuance reads 39's elephant as a counter-device. Taking 39 as the trap is plausible, so the avowal is a real development, but it rests on story context.

1172 does answer 1167: the god who freed him says Civakan removed his suffering in a dog's birth (பிணிக்குலத் தகவயிற் பிறந்த நோய்கெடுத்து). But 1167's ஊழ்வினை covers the imprisonment as well as the release, and the dog explains only the release. Teaches overstates in saying the 'former deed' is 'no hidden deed of a past birth'.
links.text_issue: 1172 line 1 பிணிக்குலத்து for the race of dogs is unusual.

links.reason: The epic gives one simile to the two women: 299 எஃகு எறி பிணையின் மாழ்கி for Vijayai at the usurper's victory drum, and 2344 வேலேறு பெற்ற பிணையின்னனி மாழ்கி for the usurper's queen at his fall. The reversal is exact: Vijayai sinks and recovers, while the other dies (இறந்து பட்டாள்), so the figure carries the wrong back to its source.

Naladiyar 17 turns வேல்கண்ணள் into கோல்கண்ணள் to warn men against desiring a woman. Manimekalai 20:40-48 has the desired woman herself show Udayakumaran an old woman, feature by feature (வெண் மணல் ஆகிய கூந்தல் ... வழுநீர் சுமந்தன), so the lesson on age becomes her own refusal, as teaches says. No gains clauses are given for this bridge.

21 has the king offer a human pair (மக்கள் இரட்டையை ஈனமில் பலியாக), and 32 has the brother say harm reaches only the body (உடம்பிற் கேதம் ... அதுநமதன்று). These are not incompatible claims about one thing: one is the rite's worth to the king, the other the victims' detachment. That the victims 'defuse the rite's meaning' is read in.
22 has the resolve (விரவிய தவத்தனாக வேண்டுவது எண்ணம்) and 23 its execution in the next verse (முனிவனம் புகுந்து ... முனிவனாய் நின்றான்). This is plot sequence; no claim is answered or reversed.

1193 is a hungry sword drinking blood (தானவர் குருதி மாந்தித் தம்பசி தணியும்), and 1199 a plough furrowing chests and sowing victory (செஞ்சால்கள் போக்கி ... வென்றி வித்தி). Feeding and ploughing are different images. Teaches makes both 'cultivation', which is true of 1199 only.

Verse 427 and Kural 686 share learning and effective speech (கற்றவன் ... உய்த்துரைக்கும் ஆற்றலான் against கற்று ... செலச்சொல்லி), so the court's choice illustrates part of the couplet. Teaches and the epic-side gain rest only on what 427 leaves out (fearlessness, timing), an argument from silence that names no limit or test. That is agreement in part, not development.

1508 lists a cakravartin's treasures (எழுவகை அருங்கலம் இரண்டு மாநிதி ... நகர்களும் வேந்தர் கூட்டமும), and Kural 381 the six limbs of a state (படைகுடி கூழ்அமைச்சு நட்பரண்). Two different lists on the topic of royal possession neither limit nor answer each other, and each 'gain' is only the other's different items.

Both promise a height beyond rebirth: Kural 346's வானோர்க்கு உயர்ந்த உலகம் for cutting யான் எனது, and 2988's மேலுலகின் உச்சி ஏமஞ்சால் இன்பம் for crossing தொல்வினை. This is close agreement, but teaches only says each fills the other's gap, and the 'location at the top of the universe' is the Jain cosmology read into the couplet.

467 has the city women wonder whose penance won them the hero (அண்ணலைத் தவத்திற் றந்தார் யார்கொலோ), and 29 says Civakan, having tasted a greater sweetness, no longer wants women (முலை போகம் வேண்டான்). These do not make incompatible claims about one thing. 29 never uses தவம், so 'the word தவம் is turned against the hope' is false.

641 has the king order counsel (அமைச்சர்கள் ஓதி யாங்குணர்ந்து ஈக), and Kural 445 is about choosing one's counsellors with care (சூழ்வாரைச் சூழ்ந்து கொளல்). The claimed limit, counsel asked only after the decision, rests on verses 634-640, which the packet does not print and which the marker hedges ('may be formal'). 641 itself shows no such limit.

Acuvakanthan's boast (மேருத் துளங்குமோ ... மானிடப் பேதைகள் ஆற்றலால்) and Naladiyar 3's mighty kings who fall when deeds turn (வினைஉலப்ப வேறாகி வீழ்வர்) share only the theme of pride before a fall. The verse does not limit the quatrain, and teaches reads the later fall into the boast. Neither gain names more than the shared theme.

The shared image is exact: 192 களிக் கயல் பொருவ ... கண்ணாள் and Naladiyar 44 பொருகயல் among the praises the renouncer refuses (கண்ணில்புன் மாக்கள்). But the epic's narrator praises; it makes no claim that the quatrain denies, so this is a meaningful same image (stock praise recast as snare) rather than a tension. The king's fall follows in the story, not in 192.

The two share wording closely: Innaa 22 ஊனைத்தின் றூனைப் பெருக்குதல் and Kural 251 தன்னூன் பெருக்கற்குத் தான்பிறிது ஊனுண்பான், and the agreement across books is real. But teaches says the act is ranked above 'kingless armies'. Line 1 யானையின் மன்னர் is kings without elephants.
links.text_issue: Innaa 22 line 4 has a source variant (கானாறு).

links.reason: NKK 170 names fear of an evil rebirth in general (தீக்கதிப் பிறவிக்கு அஞ்சி) and names no deed. Naladiyar 85's eunuch rebirth for adultery (பிறர்மனைமேல் சென்றாரே ... அலியாகி) is one arbitrary instance among many that could be paired. Calling the adultery penalty 'the ground of a whole poem's moral' is unsupported.

2502 is a decorative conceit about a necklace and makes no claim. Teaches itself admits 'the festive verse itself does not say' what the quatrain opposes. Naladiyar 120's warning (போற்றிப் புனைந்த உடம்பும் பயமின்றே) has no incompatible claim to meet, so the tension is a shared topic, adornment of the body.

304 reports kings paying tribute in fear (நலிதல் அஞ்சித் திறைகொடுத்து), and 690 has the prince defy the demand (திறையினை மறுத்தவர் திறத்துச் செய்வதோர் முறையுளதெனின்). This is a plot contrast, not incompatible claims, and it is a courtier's report set against a later act.

The echo is pointed: 138 வெங்கண் யானை வேந்து இறைஞ்ச வென்றியின் விளங்கினான and 159 நகை வேலினால் ... நின்றனர் வெங்கண் யானை விளங்கொளி வேந்தரே. The same kings bow first to the father's victory and then to the daughter's smile-spear. This is a meaningful shared figure, not a development of one claim by another, so it would be sound as same_image.

540 has the king keep the suitors in suspense (ஆசையுள் அரசர் நிற்ப ... காதலுங் கரந்து வைத்தான்), and 613 has the Avanti king arrive. This is narrative sequence. Neither verse names the city or the horoscope's choice of it, so teaches's 'unknowing escorts to the city where her destined husband lives' is supplied from outside both.

2077 answers 904 in so many words: the mother told the father of the girl's anger at Civakan over the powder (சுண்ண மாலையோ டிகலித் தோற்றாள் ... சீவகன் றிறத்திற் காய்ந்தாள்), and she now says the man who spoiled her powder (சுண்ணம் வாட்டினன்) has won her. Her குறைவி ... காத்த கற்பிது போலும rereads the grievance as chastity kept for him, so the earlier unit is reversed.

2911 forbids a king even one false syllable for fear of losing fame (நொடியலோ ரெழுத்தும் பொய்யை ... அரும்புகழ் கெடுதல் அஞ்சி), and Kural 292 lets a lie stand as truth if its good is faultless (புரைதீர்ந்த நன்மை பயக்கும் எனின்). The two can be reconciled: the epic's rule is for a king whose word is watched, and the couplet's exception is narrow. The pair reads better as the epic narrowing the exception for a ruler, and the note does not say which reading the conflict needs.

547 has Nami bow to the serpent king (பணதரற் பணிந்து) and ask for wish-granting wealth (வேண்டிய விளைக்குஞ் செல்வம்), not a yogi. Teaches places the request 'at the feet of a yogi', and the other-side gain says he 'gets it', which 547 does not state. The Tirumanthiram's ranking (மாதவம் ... பிறப்பினை நீக்கும்) is imposed on a verse that, as the marker notes, makes no judgment of the wish.
